title: Anomaly alert orchestration: suppression, enrichment, and SLA-aware severity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The console analytics pipeline already surfaces anomaly candidates for usage/cost/latency via the metrics-ingest -> anomaly-candidates Kafka topic and a lightweight scoring model. We lack a robust orchestration layer to convert candidates into reliable, actionable alerts. Observed issues: noisy duplicates across regions/routes, repeated low-value notifications during transient spikes, and mismapped severity that ignores customer SLAs and reserved capacity tiers.

Goal: Build an orchestration service (anomaly-orchestrator) that consumes candidate signals, attaches contextual enrichment, applies dynamic suppression/dedup rules, maps to SLA-aware severity, and routes proven alerts to downstream channels (Slack, PagerDuty, email). The service should be observable, testable offline, and integrate with existing pipeline stores (ClickHouse / metrics-store).

Scope & approach:
- Ingest: read from anomaly-candidates topic. Support batch and streaming read modes.
- Enrichment: attach metadata per candidate - customer_id, tier (hosted/dedicated/private), model_id, route_id, region, recent deploys (from deploy-events), and active rollout flags. Enrichment uses existing console metadata service with a local cache and fallbacks to ClickHouse for historical joins.
- Suppression/Grouping: implement time-window based suppression with adaptive cooldowns (shorter cooldowns for low-impact customers, longer for enterprise P0s). Group duplicates using a composite key (customer_id, metric_type, route_id, model_id) with fuzzy matching on metric dimensions to avoid splitting semantically identical alerts.
- SLA-aware severity: compute severity (P0/P1/P2) by combining absolute metric delta, baseline deviation, and customer SLA tier + route SLO. For example, a 5% latency increase for a P0 route of an enterprise customer escalates to P0 regardless of magnitude.
- Routing & Escalation: map severity to channels and policies. P0 -> PagerDuty escalation + #console-incidents Slack channel; P1 -> Slack with on-call CC, P2 -> daily digest/email. Attach runbook links and a minimal set of diagnostic fields (recent traces link, top offending requests, model version).
- Enrichment for triage: persist enriched alert events to ClickHouse for offline analysis and support generating alert evaluation traces for product/SE triage.
- Testing & safety: include an offline replay mode to verify suppression rules and enrichment changes using a month of historical candidate data. Add canary gating before enabling PagerDuty routing.

Acceptance criteria:
- The orchestrator consumes anomaly-candidates and emits deduplicated alerts to the alerts topic within 3s median processing time under normal load.
- Duplicate alerts reduced by >=60% on our sampled week of noisy deploys compared to current baseline.
- Severity mapping includes customer SLA and produces expected severity for 10 representative cases (unit tests + replay).
- PagerDuty routing disabled behind a kill switch for first rollout; Slack digests enabled for early beta customers.
- End-to-end integration test + replay harness committed and documented.

Trade-offs & decisions considered:
- We can co-locate enrichment with the scoring model to avoid extra hops, but opted for a separate enrichment layer to keep scoring stateless and allow independent scaling.
- Adaptive cooldown logic will start conservative (longer cooldown) and be tuned with telemetry; initial rollout will rely on per-customer defaults to avoid missed incidents.
- Grouping will use deterministic composite keys rather than ML clustering to simplify explainability for SRE/SE teams.

Open questions:
- Should we prioritize route-level or model-level deduping when both change together during deploys? Current plan: prefer route-level grouping, but add an option to escalate to model-level group when model delta > threshold.
- What privacy constraints apply when enriching with deploy metadata for private on-prem customers? We will gate enrichment fields by customer privacy flags from the metadata service.

Implementation notes / components to deliver:
- anomaly-orchestrator service (Go) with Kafka consumer, enrichment client, suppression engine, alert router.
- ClickHouse schema for enriched_alerts and orchestrator_metrics.
- Replay/validation tool that can consume historical topics and produce suppression/evaluation reports.
- Configuration UI hooks in Console for enabling PagerDuty per-customer and adjusting suppression windows.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge core orchestrator behind feature flag; enable read-only mode writing to enriched_alerts only.
2) Run replay validation for 30 days of data and iterate rules.
3) Enable Slack routing for beta customers.
4) After 2 weeks of stable beta (false positive rate < 10%), enable PagerDuty by customer opt-in.
